# Condition-Based Intrusion Detection System for Audio/Video Recording and Communication Devices

## Overview

Modern security systems can be enhanced through the implementation of intelligent intrusion zones that work in conjunction with audio/video (A/V) recording and communication devices. This system leverages a network device to store, process, and act upon data in a manner that enables customized, condition-based security responses to detected motion events.

## Data Storage and Configuration

At the core of this system, a network device stores data associated with an intrusion zone that is monitored by an audio/video recording and communication device. This stored data includes two key components: a conditional setting that defines the parameters under which the system should respond, and at least one designated action that the security system should perform when those parameters are met. By storing this configuration information, the network device establishes a framework for evaluating and responding to security events within the defined zone.

## Motion Detection and Data Reception

When the audio/video recording and communication device detects movement within its monitored area, it transmits motion data to the network device. This motion data indicates that motion was detected within the intrusion zone, providing the network device with the information necessary to initiate its evaluation process. This communication between the A/V device and the network device forms the critical link that allows real-time security monitoring.

## Conditional Evaluation

Upon receiving the motion data, the network device performs an evaluation to determine whether the conditional setting associated with the intrusion zone has been satisfied. This step is essential to the system's intelligent functionality, as it allows the network device to distinguish between motion events that warrant a response and those that do not. Rather than reacting to every detected movement, the system applies the predefined conditions to make a more nuanced determination.

## Action Execution

When the network device determines that the conditional setting has been satisfied, it causes the security system to perform the designated action. This action may take various forms depending on the configuration, such as activating an alarm to alert occupants or deter potential intruders. By tying specific responses to specific conditions, the system ensures that security actions are both appropriate and proportionate to the detected event.

## System Purpose and Benefits

Taken as a whole, this system is designed to create intrusion zones that enable customized, condition-based security responses to detected motion. This approach moves beyond simple motion detection by allowing users to define precisely when and how the security system should respond. The result is a more flexible, intelligent, and effective security solution that can be tailored to the unique needs of any monitored environment.

# Creating Intrusion Zones for Enhanced Security System Automation

## Overview

This application relates to the field of security systems and, more specifically, to methods and systems for creating and managing intrusion zones that enable more intelligent and context-aware security automation. By linking the motion detection capabilities of audio/video recording and communication devices to conditional logic and predefined security actions, the disclosed technology provides a more responsive and adaptable approach to property protection.

## Background

Traditional security systems often operate on relatively simple detection-and-response models. When a sensor detects motion or an intrusion, the system typically triggers a uniform response regardless of the surrounding circumstances. This lack of contextual awareness can lead to false alarms, unnecessary alerts, and inefficient security responses. There exists a need for security systems capable of evaluating the conditions under which motion is detected and tailoring their responses accordingly.

## Summary of the Technology

The present application addresses these challenges by introducing a framework for creating intrusion zones supported by conditional logic. Central to this technology is a network device that stores data establishing relationships between three key elements: (1) the detection of motion by an audio/video recording device within a defined zone, (2) one or more conditional settings that must be satisfied, and (3) corresponding security actions to be executed when those conditions are met.

## Detailed Description

### System Architecture

The system comprises a network device configured to store and process data associations. This network device maintains records that link the motion detection functionality of an audio/video recording and communication device—such as a video doorbell, security camera, or similar apparatus—to specific intrusion zones. Each zone represents a designated physical area monitored by the recording device.

For each defined zone, the network device stores conditional settings that govern when a security response should be triggered. These conditional settings introduce a layer of intelligence to the system, allowing it to evaluate contextual factors before initiating an action. Conditional settings may include, for example, the time of day, the armed or disarmed state of the security system, the presence or absence of authorized individuals, or other environmental or situational parameters.

### Operational Flow

In operation, the audio/video recording device monitors its assigned zones for movement. When motion is detected within a particular zone, the recording device generates motion data and transmits this information to the network device. This motion data indicates that movement has occurred within the boundaries of the specified intrusion zone.

Upon receiving the motion data, the network device performs an evaluation. It identifies the zone associated with the detected motion and retrieves the corresponding conditional setting linked to that zone. The network device then determines whether the conditional setting has been satisfied based on the current circumstances.

If the network device confirms that the conditional setting is satisfied, it proceeds to trigger the security system to perform the designated security action. This action may take various forms depending on the configuration, such as activating an alarm, sending a notification to a user or monitoring service, illuminating lights, locking or unlocking doors, or initiating recording by additional devices.

### Advantages

By incorporating conditional logic into the intrusion detection process, this technology enables more contextual and responsive security automation. Rather than responding uniformly to all detected motion, the system can differentiate between benign and threatening circumstances, reducing false alarms and ensuring that security responses are appropriate to the situation. This selective, condition-based approach enhances both the effectiveness and the user experience of the security system, providing property owners with greater control and confidence in their protective measures.

## Conclusion

The disclosed methods and systems represent a meaningful advancement in security automation technology. By linking motion detection within defined zones to conditional settings and corresponding security actions through a network device, the application delivers a flexible, intelligent framework capable of adapting its responses to real-world conditions—ultimately providing more reliable and contextually appropriate security protection.

# Patent Abstract

**System and Method for Creating Intrusion Zones Using Audio/Video Recording and Communication Devices**

## Abstract

A system and method for creating and managing intrusion zones within a security system utilizing audio/video recording and communication (A/V) devices is disclosed. The system comprises one or more A/V devices, each including a camera, a microphone, a motion sensor, and a communication module configured to communicate over a network with a backend server and a client device associated with a user. The system enables a user to define one or more intrusion zones within a field of view of the A/V device, wherein each intrusion zone corresponds to a designated spatial region to be monitored for unauthorized entry or activity.

In operation, the A/V device captures image data and detects motion within its field of view. A processor analyzes the captured data to determine whether a detected object or subject has entered a defined intrusion zone. Upon determining that an intrusion event has occurred within the designated zone, the system generates an alert and transmits a notification to the client device and/or the backend server. The system may further activate one or more security responses, including recording audio/video data, activating a siren or illumination device, or communicating with a monitoring service or law enforcement.

The intrusion zones may be user-configurable through a graphical user interface presented on the client device, allowing the user to establish boundaries, sensitivity levels, active time schedules, and associated response actions for each zone. By defining discrete intrusion zones, the system reduces false alerts caused by activity in non-monitored areas and enhances the accuracy and efficiency of security monitoring.

---

*Note: This is a sample abstract for illustrative and drafting purposes. Actual patent abstracts should be prepared or reviewed by a registered patent attorney or agent and tailored to the specific claims and technical details of the invention.*

# Intelligent Video Surveillance System with Configurable Intrusion Detection Zones

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to video surveillance systems, and more particularly to an intelligent security camera system configured to define spatial intrusion zones and to selectively trigger alarm conditions based upon the satisfaction of one or more predetermined criteria.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional security camera systems are known to generate alarm notifications upon the detection of motion within a monitored field of view. Such systems, however, are prone to generating false positive alarms in response to inconsequential events, including without limitation environmental movement, transient illumination changes, and the presence of authorized persons or objects. There exists a need in the art for a surveillance system capable of discriminating between events of interest and events of no consequence through the application of configurable spatial and conditional parameters.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with one embodiment of the present invention, there is provided a security camera system comprising:

**(a)** at least one image capture device configured to acquire a plurality of image frames representative of a monitored physical environment;

**(b)** a processing unit operatively coupled to said image capture device;

**(c)** a non-transitory computer-readable medium having stored thereon instructions executable by said processing unit; and

**(d)** a user interface configured to receive one or more zone definition inputs from an operator.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### Zone Configuration

In a preferred embodiment, the system is configured to receive, via said user interface, at least one **intrusion zone definition** comprising a set of coordinate data delineating a bounded polygonal region within the field of view of said image capture device. Said bounded region may be defined by an operator through the manipulation of a plurality of vertices superimposed upon a representative image frame, whereby said vertices collectively establish a perimeter enclosing a designated area of interest.

Each said intrusion zone may be associated with one or more **conditional parameters**, wherein said conditional parameters comprise, without limitation:

**(i)** a **temporal parameter** defining one or more time intervals during which said zone is to be maintained in an active monitoring state;

**(ii)** an **object classification parameter** specifying one or more categories of detected objects that shall be deemed eligible to trigger an alarm condition, said categories including without limitation a human person, a vehicle, or an animal;

**(iii)** a **dwell-time parameter** specifying a minimum duration for which a detected object must remain within said bounded region prior to the initiation of an alarm condition;

**(iv)** a **directional parameter** specifying a permissible or impermissible direction of traversal across a boundary of said bounded region; and

**(v)** a **dimensional parameter** specifying a minimum or maximum size threshold of a detected object.

### Detection and Evaluation Logic

In operation, said processing unit is configured to analyze said plurality of image frames to detect the presence of one or more objects within said monitored environment. Upon detection of an object at least partially coincident with a defined intrusion zone, said processing unit is further configured to evaluate whether said detected object satisfies the conditional parameters associated with said zone.

The system may be configured such that an alarm condition is triggered **only upon the concurrent satisfaction** of a plurality of said conditional parameters. By way of illustration and not limitation, the system may be configured to trigger an alarm condition solely in response to the detection of an object classified as a human person, traversing a boundary of said bounded region in a specified direction, during a specified temporal interval, and remaining within said region for a duration exceeding said dwell-time parameter.

In a further embodiment, the system comprises logic for combining a plurality of conditional parameters through the application of Boolean operators, whereby an operator may specify logical relationships, including conjunctive (AND), disjunctive (OR), and negation (NOT) relationships, among said parameters.

### Alarm Response

Upon determination that the requisite conditions have been satisfied, said processing unit is configured to initiate at least one responsive action, said responsive action comprising one or more of: transmitting a notification to a remote device, activating an audible or visual annunciator, recording a video segment corresponding to the triggering event, and storing metadata descriptive of said event.

## CLAIMS

**What is claimed is:**

**1.** A security camera system comprising: an image capture device; a processing unit; and a memory storing instructions that, when executed, cause the processing unit to: define an intrusion zone within a field of view of said image capture device; associate said intrusion zone with a plurality of conditional parameters; detect an object within said intrusion zone; and trigger an alarm condition only upon determination that said detected object satisfies said plurality of conditional parameters.

**2.** The system of claim 1, wherein said plurality of conditional parameters comprises a temporal parameter, an object classification parameter, and a dwell-time parameter.

**3.** The system of claim 1, wherein said processing unit is further configured to evaluate said plurality of conditional parameters in accordance with one or more operator-defined Boolean relationships.

---

*This document is provided as an illustrative example of patent-style drafting and does not constitute a filed or filable patent application or legal advice.*
